source: https://pichenettes.github.io/mutable-instruments-documentation/ (the Mutable Instruments manuals, which vcvrack.com/AudibleInstruments links to) with https://github.com/VCVRack/AudibleInstruments v2.0.0 as the authority where they differ

lines: Digital oscillator carrying 48 synthesis models, from analogue waveforms and wavetables to physical models, speech and drum circuits, each shaped by two parameters
Steps through the 48 models; the four-letter code of the one in use shows on the display
Detunes by up to a semitone either way
Sets the pitch in octaves, from five octaves below the middle C of the oscillator to three above it
Attenuverts the FM input, which shifts the pitch by one octave per volt at full clockwise; with META switched on it scales that input's control of the model instead
Sets the first shaping parameter of the model in use, which is the waveform sweep, the wavefolder amount, the sync interval or the filter cutoff depending on which model that is
Attenuverts the TIMBRE input, which adds to the TIMBRE knob
Sets the second shaping parameter of the model in use, which is the detuning, the feedback amount, the formant shift or the brightness depending on which model that is
A rising edge past 1V strikes the physical models, resets the phase of the other models and fires the internal envelope
Sets the pitch, one volt per octave, added to the two frequency knobs
Shifts the pitch, scaled and inverted by the FM knob, one octave per volt at full clockwise
Adds to the TIMBRE knob through the MODULATION attenuverter, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the COLOR knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
The oscillator, peaking at 5V, though loudness differs from model to model
Menu — Model picks the synthesis model from a list that names what each one does
Menu — META: FM CV selects model hands the FM input over to choosing the model, and pitch is then set by V/OCT and the frequency knobs alone
Menu — DRFT: Pitch drift adds the slow random detuning of an analogue oscillator
Menu — SIGN: Waveform imperfections mixes in a waveshaped copy of the output for a dirtier tone
Menu — Low CPU (disable resampling) runs the oscillator at the engine sample rate instead of resampling from 96kHz, which costs less processing and adds aliasing
Digital oscillator with sixteen models in two banks, eight pitched and eight noise or percussive, each shaped by three parameters and played through a built-in envelope and low-pass gate
Selects the bank of eight pitched models, and each further press steps to the next model in it
Selects the bank of eight noise and percussive models, and each further press steps to the next model in it
Sets the pitch, four octaves either side of the centre
Sets the harmonic content of the model in use: the detuning, the chord, the number of partials or the filter resonance, depending on which model that is
Sets the main timbre parameter of the model in use, which brightens or dirties the tone in a way particular to each one
Morphs the model in use along a second axis: the waveform, the formant or the noise colour, depending on which model that is
Attenuverts the TIMBRE input
Attenuverts the FM input, which shifts the pitch by six semitones per volt at full clockwise
Attenuverts the MORPH input
Sets how much the low-pass gate darkens the sound as it closes, from a plain fall in level to a filter closing with it; it appears in place of the TIMBRE knob when LPG editing is on
Sets the decay time of the internal envelope and low-pass gate that a trigger fires; it appears in place of the MORPH knob when LPG editing is switched on in the menu
Offsets the model away from the one the buttons choose; while TRIG is patched the voltage here is read at each trigger
Adds to the TIMBRE knob through its attenuverter, 8V covering the whole knob range
Shifts the pitch, scaled by the FM attenuverter, six semitones per volt at full clockwise
Adds to the MORPH knob through its attenuverter, 8V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the HARMONICS knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
A pulse past about 0.7V strikes the model and fires the internal envelope and low-pass gate
Sets the level of the low-pass gate, 8V for full; while it is patched the gate follows this voltage rather than the internal envelope alone
Sets the pitch, one volt per octave; the number of channels on this cable sets how many voices the module runs, up to sixteen
The main signal of the model in use, peaking at 5V
A second signal from the same model, which is a sub-oscillator, a second formant or a different part of the drum, depending on which model is in use
Menu — the two model lists pick the model by name, with the pitched models and the noise and percussive models in separate groups
Menu — Edit LPG response/decay swaps the TIMBRE and MORPH knobs for the low-pass gate's response and decay knobs
Menu — Low CPU (disable resampling) runs the oscillator at the engine sample rate instead of resampling from 48kHz, which costs less processing and adds aliasing
Physical-modelling voice: three exciters — bowing, blowing and striking — feeding a bank of tuned resonant modes, with a stereo reverb after it
Sets the shape of the envelope applied to the bow and blow exciters, running from short decays through slower sustained shapes to fast attack-release shapes
Sets how much bowing noise reaches the resonator, raising the simulated bow pressure with it so the tone grows brighter and grittier
Sets how much granular blowing noise reaches the resonator
Sets how much percussive noise reaches the resonator; past about two o'clock some of it also bleeds straight to the output for a harder attack
Sets the fundamental in semitone steps, spanning five octaves
Detunes the fundamental by up to two semitones either way
Attenuverts the FM input, on an exponential scale that stays gentle near the centre
Sets the colour of the blowing noise, scanning a range of noise textures
Chooses what the striking exciter hits with, morphing through recorded mallets, modelled mallets, plectrums and bouncing particles
Sets the shape and stiffness of the resonating structure, from plates through strings to bars and tubes to bells and bowls
Sets how much the high modes are damped, low settings giving wood or nylon and high settings glass or steel
Sets the smoothness or granularity of the bowing noise
Sets the pitch and granulation rate of the blowing noise
Sets the brightness and speed of the percussive excitation
Sets how fast the resonator loses energy, which is how long a note rings on
Sets where on the string or surface the excitation is applied; in the middle the even harmonics cancel and the tone goes hollow
Sets the stereo width below noon and the amount and decay of the reverb above it
Attenuverts the bow timbre input
Attenuverts the air flow input
Attenuverts the blow timbre input
Attenuverts the mallet input
Attenuverts the strike timbre input
Attenuverts the damping input
Attenuverts the geometry input
Attenuverts the position input
Attenuverts the brightness input
Attenuverts the reverb space input
Runs the exciter and its envelope for as long as the button is held, which is what a high gate on the GATE input does
Sets the fundamental of the resonator, one volt per octave; the number of channels on this cable sets how many voices the module runs, up to sixteen
Shifts the fundamental, scaled by the FM attenuverter
A voltage of 1V or more runs the exciter and its envelope
Attenuates the excitation, full strength at 0V and silent at 5V
An external signal that takes the place of the blowing noise, passing through the envelope and the strength control on its way to the resonator
An external signal sent straight into the resonator with no processing before it
Modulates the bow timbre through its attenuverter
Modulates the colour of the blowing noise through its attenuverter
Modulates the blow timbre through its attenuverter
Modulates the mallet type through its attenuverter
Modulates the strike timbre through its attenuverter
Modulates the damping through its attenuverter
Modulates the resonator geometry through its attenuverter
Modulates the excitation position through its attenuverter
Modulates the brightness through its attenuverter
Modulates the reverb space through its attenuverter; a large voltage with the SPACE knob at maximum freezes the reverb tail
The resonator signal; as SPACE is raised this becomes the left half of a stereo pair
The exciter signal; as SPACE is raised this becomes the right half of a stereo pair
Menu — Models chooses the resonator: the original, a non-linear string, chords, or the Ominous voice
Elements.notes: Which output carries which signal was settled from the Mutable resonator code: at minimum SPACE the left jack carries the resonator and the right jack the raw exciter. Strength is inverted relative to the hardware: the Mutable manual describes positive CV boosting the excitation, while the plugin computes 1 minus the voltage over 5, so 0V gives full strength and 5V silences it. The plugin behaviour is what the line describes.

lines: Shape generator that runs as an LFO, an audio oscillator or a one-shot AD or AR envelope, with the wave adjustable in curvature, rise-to-fall balance and harmonic content
Cycles the generator between a one-shot AD envelope, free-running cycles and a one-shot AR envelope
Cycles the frequency range between low, medium and high, the high range using waveshapes and a slope response chosen for audio rates
Sets the rate, four octaves either side of the middle of the chosen range
Attenuverts the FM input; with nothing patched there that input reads a constant 0.1V, so the knob works as a fine frequency control
Sets the curvature of the rising and falling segments, stepping through a set of paired shapes
Sets the split between rise and fall time: fully counter-clockwise the rise is instant, at noon they are equal, fully clockwise the fall is instant
Low-pass filters the wave counter-clockwise of noon and wavefolds it clockwise of noon
Adds to the SHAPE knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the SLOPE knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the SMOOTHNESS knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
A voltage of 0.7V or more starts the envelope in AD or AR mode, and resets the phase in cyclic mode
A voltage of 0.7V or more stops the wave where it is until the voltage falls again
Sets the rate, one volt per octave
Shifts the rate, scaled by the FM attenuverter
Scales the UNI and BI outputs like a VCA, 8V giving full level; with nothing patched it reads 8V
Locks the rate to an external clock whenever a cable is patched here, the FREQUENCY knob then setting the ratio between that clock and the output; it reads high at 0.7V
Carries 5V while the wave is rising and 0V from the end of the rise until the cycle starts again
Carries 5V until the fall has finished, then 0V until the next cycle or trigger
The wave as a unipolar signal, 0-8V
The wave as a bipolar signal, -5V to 5V, with a positive and a negative bump in each cycle rather than a shifted copy of the unipolar wave
Menu — Wavetable firmware (Sheep) swaps the generator for the Sheep firmware, which scans wavetables, and changes the panel with it
Segment generator running as an LFO, an audio oscillator or a one-shot AD or AR envelope, with four outputs that can differ in waveshape, level, timing or frequency
Sets what the middle of the FREQUENCY knob means: 1/8Hz for slow movement, 2Hz for modulation, or 130.8Hz for audible tones
Cycles how the four outputs relate: four waveshapes from points along the signal chain, one signal crossfaded between them, a time shift spread across them, or a frequency ratio between them
Cycles the generator between a one-shot AD envelope, free-running cycles and a one-shot AR envelope
Sets the rate, four octaves either side of the centre set by the range button; clockwise is faster, so a one-shot envelope grows shorter
Sets the curvature of the rising and falling segments
Low-pass filters the wave counter-clockwise of noon and wavefolds it clockwise of noon
Sets how the cycle time is divided between the rising and the falling segment
In the first output mode it attenuverts the main signal; in the others it sets what separates the outputs — which one the signal goes to, how far their peaks shift in time, or their frequency ratio
Attenuverts the SLOPE input
Attenuverts the FREQUENCY input
Attenuverts the SMOOTHNESS input
Attenuverts the SHAPE input
Attenuverts the SHIFT/LEVEL input
Adds to the SLOPE knob through its attenuverter, 10V covering the whole knob range
Shifts the rate through its attenuverter, twelve semitones per volt at full clockwise
Sets the rate, one volt per octave
Adds to the SMOOTHNESS knob through its attenuverter, 10V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the SHAPE knob through its attenuverter, 10V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the SHIFT/LEVEL knob through its attenuverter, 10V covering the whole knob range
A rising edge past 1.7V starts an AD envelope or resets the cycle; in AR mode the envelope rises while the gate is high and falls when it goes low
Locks the rate to an external clock whenever a cable is patched here, the FREQUENCY knob then setting the ratio; it reads high at 1.7V
The first of the four related signals; in the amplitude output mode the SHIFT/LEVEL knob attenuverts this one
One of the signals following the first, differing from it in waveshape, level, timing or frequency according to the output mode
Granular texture synthesizer: incoming stereo audio is recorded into a buffer and replayed as a cloud of grains, with feedback and reverb after it
Stops new audio being recorded, so the grains carry on from what is already in the buffer
Steps the BLEND knob and the BLEND input through the four things they can control: dry and wet balance, stereo spread, feedback and reverb
Sets how far back in the recorded buffer grains are taken from, clockwise reaching further into the past
Sets the length of each grain
Transposes the grains, two octaves either way
Sets the level of the signal written into the buffer
At noon no grains are sown; clockwise they are sown at random times and counter-clockwise at a steady rate, overlapping more the further the knob is turned
Morphs the shape of the grain envelope from a rectangle through a triangle to a bell curve, and past two o'clock brings in a diffuser that smears transients
Crossfades between the dry input and the granulated signal
Sets how widely the grains are scattered across the stereo field; it appears in place of the BLEND knob when the mode button selects spread
Sets how much of the output is written back into the buffer; it appears in place of the BLEND knob when the mode button selects feedback
Sets the amount of reverb on the granulated signal; it appears in place of the BLEND knob when the mode button selects reverb
A voltage of 1V or more stops new audio being recorded
A voltage of 1V or more sows a single grain
Adds to the POSITION knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the SIZE knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Transposes the grains, one volt per octave, added to the PITCH knob
Adds to whichever of the four parameters the BLEND knob is set to, 5V covering the whole range
The left input to the buffer, scaled by the IN GAIN knob
The right input to the buffer, scaled by the IN GAIN knob; with nothing patched here the left input feeds both sides
Adds to the DENSITY knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the TEXTURE knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
The left channel of the grain cloud mixed with the dry signal
The right channel of the grain cloud mixed with the dry signal
Menu — Blend knob picks which of the four parameters the BLEND knob and its input control, the same choice the mode button steps through
Menu — Alternate mode swaps granular playback for a pitch-shifter and time-stretcher, a looping delay, or spectral processing
Menu — Quality sets the buffer's length and format, trading fidelity for recording time, from 1 second of 32kHz 16-bit stereo to 8 seconds of 16kHz 8-bit mono
Clouds.notes: The load and save button beside the mode button is drawn on the panel and configured as a parameter, but the plugin never reads it, so it has no line and no tag.

lines: Cross-modulator: two signals combined by one of nine algorithms, from crossfading and wavefolding through ring modulation and bit crushing to a twenty-band vocoder
Sweeps continuously through the nine algorithms marked around it, and in the vocoder sets the release time of its envelope followers
Sets how strongly the cross-modulation products are produced, and in the vocoder shifts the formants taken from the modulator
Switches the internal oscillator on and steps through its waveforms; with it off, the carrier input is used instead
Sets the gain of the carrier input, or the frequency of the internal oscillator over five octaves when that is running
Sets the gain of the modulator input, and gains above unity overdrive it
Adds to the carrier gain, 5V for full; with the internal oscillator running it sets that oscillator's pitch at one volt per octave
Adds to the modulator gain, 5V for full
Sweeps the algorithm, 5V covering the whole range, added to the ALGORITHM knob
Adds to the TIMBRE knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
The carrier audio; with the internal oscillator running, this signal phase-modulates it instead
The modulator audio
The two signals combined by the chosen algorithm
The sum of the carrier and modulator after their gain stages, or the bare internal oscillator when that is running
Resonator: a bank of tuned filters, sympathetic strings or plucked string models, excited by an audio input or by a burst it generates itself
Cycles the number of overlapping voices between one, two and four, so notes played in sequence can ring on over each other
Cycles the resonator between modal, sympathetic strings and modulated string
Sets the pitch over five octaves; while V/OCT is patched it snaps to semitones
Sets the frequency ratios between the partials of the modal resonator, the tuning of the sympathetic strings, or the amount of detuning and modulation of the string resonator
Sets the level of the higher harmonics, low settings giving wood or nylon and high settings glass or steel
Sets how long a note rings, from under 100ms to about 10 seconds
Sets where the excitation strikes the string or surface; in the middle the even harmonics cancel and the tone goes hollow
Attenuverts the brightness input
Attenuverts the frequency input; with nothing patched there that input reads a constant 1V, so the knob works as a fine tuning control
Attenuverts the damping input
Attenuverts the structure input
Attenuverts the position input
Modulates the brightness through its attenuverter
Shifts the pitch through its attenuverter, on an exponential scale that stays gentle near the centre
Modulates the damping through its attenuverter
Modulates the structure through its attenuverter
Modulates the excitation position through its attenuverter
A voltage of 1V or more lets the sounding voice decay and starts the next one; with nothing patched here a note change on V/OCT or a transient in the audio input does that instead
Sets the pitch of the resonator, one volt per octave
The audio that excites the resonator; with nothing patched here a pulse or burst of noise is generated at each strum
The odd-numbered partials or strings, or one of two complementary components of a single voice; with only one of the two outputs patched, it carries the whole signal
The even-numbered partials or strings, or one of two complementary components of a single voice; with only one of the two outputs patched, it carries the whole signal
Menu — Resonator picks from six models, the three on the panel plus an FM voice, quantized sympathetic strings and a reverb string
Menu — Disastrous Peace swaps the resonator for the four-voice string synthesizer hidden in the hardware, with chorus, reverb and formant effects
Three fixed utility sections: a buffered mult with one input and three outputs, a two-into-two mixer, and a three-into-one mixer
The signal copied to the three outputs of the mult section; a polyphonic cable is copied channel for channel
A copy of the signal patched into the mult section
One of the two signals the middle section adds together
The sum of the two signals patched into the middle section
One of the three signals the bottom section adds together
The sum of the three signals patched into the bottom section
Links.notes: No families: every jack carries whatever is patched into the section, audio or CV alike.

lines: Three utility sections: an inverter with two rectifiers, an analogue maximum and minimum, and a sample and hold with its own noise source
The signal the inverter and the two rectifiers work on
The input signal with its sign flipped
The input signal with everything below 0V clipped away
The size of the input signal with its sign discarded, the negative half folded upwards, which doubles the frequency of a symmetrical wave
One of the two signals the logic section compares; an unpatched input counts as 0V, so a single signal has its positive half on MAX and its negative half on MIN
The greater of the logic section's two inputs, which for gate signals is an OR
The lesser of the logic section's two inputs, which for gate signals is an AND
The signal the sample and hold reads; with nothing patched here it samples the internal noise source, giving a random voltage at each trigger
A rising edge past 0.7V makes the sample and hold take a fresh reading
White noise with a bell-shaped distribution, mostly within -2V to 2V
The voltage read at the last trigger, held until the next one
Three attenuator or attenuverter channels with chained outputs, so leaving an output unpatched sends that channel on to the one below
Sets the gain of that channel: from 0 to 1 in attenuator mode, or from -1 to 1 in attenuverter mode, where the centre mutes it
Switches that channel between an attenuator, whose gain runs from 0 to 1, and an attenuverter, whose gain runs from -1 to 1
The signal for that channel; with nothing patched it reads a constant 5V, so the knob puts out an adjustable offset instead
That channel, summed with any channel above it whose own output is unpatched
Two Bernoulli gates: each incoming gate is sent to one of two outputs on the toss of a coin, with the odds set by a knob and a CV input
Sets the odds of a gate going to the B output rather than the A output, fully clockwise sending every one to B
Switches that channel between passing the incoming gate to whichever output the coin picks, and a toggle mode where the coin chooses only whether to swap outputs and the chosen one stays high
The gate or trigger the first channel routes, read high at 2V; a polyphonic cable is tossed for channel by channel
The gate or trigger the second channel routes, read high at 2V; with nothing patched here it takes the first channel's input
Adds to that channel's probability knob, 10V covering the whole range
Carries a 10V gate when the coin sends the incoming gate to A
Carries a 10V gate when the coin sends the incoming gate to B
Four ring-modulator channels: each multiplies its input by a gain set by a knob and modulated by a CV input, with chained outputs
Sets the gain of that channel from -1 to 1, the centre muting it and counter-clockwise inverting it
Attenuverts that channel's CV input, which adds to the gain knob and can push the gain as far as -2 or 2
The signal for that channel; with nothing patched it reads a constant 5V, so the knob puts out an adjustable offset instead
Modulates that channel's gain through its attenuverter, 5V at full attenuverter changing the gain by one; with audio here and audio on the signal input the channel is a ring modulator
That channel, summed with any channel above it whose own output is unpatched
Four VCAs with adjustable response curves and chained outputs, so leaving an output unpatched sends that channel on to the one below
Sets the level of that channel; with nothing patched into its CV input this knob alone sets the gain
Sets the response of that channel's CV, exponential counter-clockwise and linear clockwise
The audio or CV for that channel
Controls the gain of that channel, 5V giving unity on the linear curve and negative voltages closing it; while it is patched the gain knob scales what it does
That channel, summed with any channel above it whose own output is unpatched
Four-channel VCA mixer whose four gains are stored in keyframes, the FRAME knob moving through the animation and interpolating between them
Sets the first channel's gain at the keyframe the FRAME knob is on, and does nothing between keyframes; in Poly LFO mode it sets the waveform of the four LFOs
Sets the second channel's gain at the keyframe the FRAME knob is on, and does nothing between keyframes; in Poly LFO mode it sets how much the waveform differs from one LFO to the next
Sets the third channel's gain at the keyframe the FRAME knob is on, and does nothing between keyframes; in Poly LFO mode it sets how far apart in frequency the four LFOs run
Sets the fourth channel's gain at the keyframe the FRAME knob is on, and does nothing between keyframes; in Poly LFO mode it sets how strongly the four LFOs pull each other into step
Stores a keyframe at the current position of the FRAME knob, holding the four gains as they stand
Removes the keyframe at the current position of the FRAME knob
Moves through the animation from its start to its end, the four gains following as it goes; in Poly LFO mode it sets the rate of the LFOs
Attenuverts the FRAME input, setting how far and in which direction a voltage moves the animation
Sends a constant 10V into the ALL input when nothing is patched there, which turns the four channels into CV sources
Feeds every channel whose own input is unpatched
The signal for that channel; with nothing patched it takes the ALL input
Moves through the animation through the MODULATION attenuverter, 10V covering the whole animation at full
The sum of the channels whose own outputs are unpatched, halved and clipped at 10V
That channel after its VCA, and patching it takes that channel out of the MIX output
Menu — Channel settings sets each channel's interpolation curve between keyframes, from step and linear to bouncing, and its response curve, linear or exponential
Menu — Clear keyframes empties the animation and leaves the four knobs in direct control of the gains
Menu — Alternate modes swaps the keyframer for a Poly LFO, four linked LFOs whose levels drive the four VCAs
Frames.notes: The FR. STEP output is drawn on the panel and configured, but the plugin never writes to it, so it has no line and no tag.

lines: Six segments that group into envelopes, sequencers and LFOs, the grouping set by which gate inputs are patched: a patched gate starts a group and every unpatched segment to its right joins it
Sets the curve of that segment when it ramps, the glide when it steps to a level, and the length when it holds
Each press steps that segment between ramping to a level, stepping to a level and waiting for a trigger, and holding a level for a set time; holding the button for a second makes it loop
Sets the time that segment takes when it ramps, and the level it goes to, 0-8V, when it steps or holds
Adds to that segment's slider, 8V covering the whole range
A gate past 1.7V runs the group of segments that begins here, and patching a cable here starts a new group
The envelope of the group that begins at this segment, or, for a segment further into a group, a ramp from 8V down to 0V while that segment is running
Random sampler: a jittery internal clock split into two streams of random gates, and three random voltages shaped by a distribution, a quantiser and a loopable memory
Switches the deja vu loop on for the gate section, so its random decisions are recycled instead of freshly drawn
Switches the deja vu loop on for the voltage section, so its random values are recycled instead of freshly drawn
Counter-clockwise of noon it sets how likely past random values are to be reused, reaching a locked loop at noon; clockwise of noon it sets how likely the loop is to jump to a random place in itself
Sets the rate of the master clock, 120 BPM at noon; with a clock patched into the t section it divides or multiplies that clock instead
Sets the width and shape of the distribution the voltages are drawn from: a fixed voltage counter-clockwise, a bell curve at noon, an even spread past that, and only the two extremes fully clockwise
Cycles how the master clock is split between the two gate outputs: a coin toss at each pulse, random multiplication and division, or an alternation like a kick and snare pattern
Cycles how the three voltage outputs answer the spread, bias and steps settings: all three alike, the outer two opposed to the middle one, or a tilt graded across them
Sets the length of the deja vu loop, from one step to sixteen
Sets how likely a gate is to land on the first gate output rather than the third
Skews the random voltages towards the bottom or the top of the range without moving the range itself
Cycles the clock range, leaving the rate as the knob sets it or dividing or multiplying it by four
Cycles the range of the random voltage outputs between 0-2V, 0-5V and -5V to 5V
Switches on external processing, where the voltage section samples whatever is patched into the X spread input instead of drawing its own random numbers
Sets how far the clock wanders from steady time, from exact through the drift of a human player to complete chaos
Counter-clockwise of noon it smooths the random voltages into slopes and curves; clockwise of noon it quantises them to a scale and then strips notes out of that scale until only the root is left
Adds to the gate bias knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the voltage bias knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
An external clock for the gate section, read high at 1.7V, taking the place of the internal one; the RATE knob then divides or multiplies it
Modulates the clock rate, each volt doubling or halving it
Adds to the JITTER knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the DEJA VU knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the STEPS knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the SPREAD knob, 5V covering the whole knob range; in external processing mode the voltage here is sampled in place of the internal random source
Clocks all three random voltage outputs together, read high at 1.7V, in place of the gates from the t section
A 10V gate whenever the master clock's pulse is sent to this output by the t section
The master clock itself, a 10V gate with an even duty cycle
A random voltage stepped at a division of the clock chosen in the menu, anywhere from a sixty-fourth of that clock to the clock itself
A random voltage drawn at each clock pulse from the distribution set by SPREAD and BIAS and shaped by STEPS
Menu — T mode reaches seven ways of splitting the clock: the three on the panel, plus independent Bernoulli, divider, three states and Markov
Menu — T range and X range set the clock division and the output voltage range, the same choices the two range buttons step through
Menu — X mode sets how the three voltage outputs answer the knobs, the same choice the X mode button steps through
Menu — Scales picks the scale the STEPS knob quantises to: major, minor, pentatonic, pelog, raag bhairav that or raag shri
Menu — Internal X clock source picks which gate outputs clock the three voltage outputs when nothing is patched into the X clock input
Menu — Y divider ratio sets how far the Y output is divided down, from the clock itself to a sixty-fourth of it
Analogue-modelled low-pass filter with two-pole and four-pole outputs, a band-pass output, and a VCA on the four-pole output
Sets the resonance, which begins to self-oscillate at about three quarters of the way up
Sets the cutoff frequency, 20Hz to 20kHz
Attenuverts the FM input, which shifts the cutoff
Adds to the resonance knob
Shifts the cutoff, one volt per octave
Shifts the cutoff through the FM attenuverter, one volt per octave at full clockwise
The audio to be filtered; the number of channels on this cable sets how many voices the module runs, up to sixteen
Sets the gain of the VCA output, 0V silencing it and 5V giving unity, with higher voltages progressively compressed; with nothing patched it reads 12V
The two-pole band-pass tap, falling away at 12dB per octave on both sides
The two-pole low-pass tap, 12dB per octave
The four-pole low-pass output, 24dB per octave
The four-pole low-pass output through the VCA, whose gain the GAIN input sets
Four-band equaliser — a low shelf, two parametric bands and a high shelf — with the high-pass, band-pass and low-pass taps of both parametric filters brought out separately
Sets the corner frequency of the high shelf, 20Hz to 20kHz, above which the shelf gain applies
Boosts or cuts everything above the high shelf's corner frequency by up to 18dB, flat at the centre
Sets the centre frequency of the first parametric band, 20Hz to 20kHz
Boosts or cuts the first parametric band by up to 18dB, flat at the centre
Sets how narrow the first parametric band is, a Q of 0.5 to 40
Sets the centre frequency of the second parametric band, 20Hz to 20kHz
Boosts or cuts the second parametric band by up to 18dB, flat at the centre
Sets how narrow the second parametric band is, a Q of 0.5 to 40
Sets the corner frequency of the low shelf, 20Hz to 20kHz, below which the shelf gain applies
Boosts or cuts everything below the low shelf's corner frequency by up to 18dB, flat at the centre
Shifts the high shelf's corner frequency, one volt per octave
